text:
morgan: Acme reports intermittent 502s and high p99 earlier today. They say their app logs don't contain any request ids. Can we draft a tiny, copy-paste checklist for them to run so we can pull traces quickly?

priya: Here's a compact checklist. Focus on the exact fields we need: UTC time window, SDK/lang+version (or curl), the request payload shape, full response headers (where the request-id lives), Console request link or debug bundle, and whether the call used streaming or function-calls. Keep it short so product folks can follow.

jin: Add a curl that writes headers to a file and a one-liner for browser fetch + mobile logs. Also remind them not to paste API keys.

morgan: Pasteable message for the customer (one block they can drop into support):

---
Hi — thanks for the report. To help us reproduce and locate logs, please provide the items below. You can paste everything here or attach a Redwood debug bundle from the Console.

1) UTC time window when you saw the error or latency spike (example: 2025-04-02 09:05:00 to 2025-04-02 09:10:00)
2) Client environment: SDK/language + exact version (e.g., node 18 + @redwood/sdk 1.5.0), browser or mobile SDK, or note if you used curl.
3) Endpoint + model + HTTP method (e.g., POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate, model: redwood-1). If this is Dedicated/Private include region or VPC name.
4) One representative request body (redact any PII). We need the prompt shape and key params: max_tokens, temperature, streaming, function-calls, etc.
5) Full HTTP response headers from a failing request — look for any of: X-Redwood-Request-Id, x-request-id, trace-id, traceparent. Quick capture options below:

- curl (headers to stdout):
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REPLACE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"test"}'
```
Look for: X-Redwood-Request-Id: 01Fxxxxxx

- curl (save headers to file):
```
curl -s -D headers.txt -o /dev/null -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REPLACE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"test"}'
cat headers.txt | grep -i request-id
```

- Browser fetch (copy this into console):
```
fetch(url, opts).then(r => { console.log('status', r.status); console.log('x-redwood-request-id', r.headers.get('x-redwood-request-id') || r.headers.get('x-request-id')); return r.text(); }).then(console.log)
```

- Node (fetch/axios):
```
const r = await fetch(url, opts);
console.log('status', r.status, 'x-redwood-request-id', r.headers.get('x-redwood-request-id') || r.headers.get('x-request-id'))
```

- Python (requests):
```
resp = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload)
print('status', resp.status_code)
print('x-redwood-request-id', resp.headers.get('x-redwood-request-id') or resp.headers.get('x-request-id'))
```

6) If latency is the issue, tell us whether you used streaming and the client-side timing you measured. Include HTTP status codes.
7) Console path: Console -> Observability -> Requests. Filter to your time window, click the request row, then choose "Copy request id" (or open details and Export debug bundle). Paste the Request ID or attach the bundle here.
8) Optional but helpful: re-run the failing request once (replace API key with REDACTED_API_KEY) and paste the exact response headers — that lets us match traces immediately.

Security note: Please scrub any PII from payloads before pasting. Request IDs and trace IDs are safe to share and are the single fastest way for us to find backend logs.

If you share the Request ID + UTC window we'll pull the trace and reply with findings.
---

jin: Extra internal tip we can add when routing: ask the customer to include the client timestamp and the HTTP status shown on the client. Those two values speed up CDN/edge correlation.
